basis: Severe intellectual disability defines the syndrome; strabismus affects 80-99%, impairing ocular alignment.
Osteoporosis, joint hyperlaxity and congenital blindness define the syndrome; intellectual disability is reported without a reliable frequency.
Medial deviation of one or both eyes is an ocular motility disorder.
Congenital ineffective erythropoiesis and hemolytic anemia; hepatomegaly and bilirubin elevation alone do not establish direct hepatic injury.
Hindbrain dysplasia and cranial neuropathies define PTCD; sensorineural hearing loss occurs in most patients, commonly exceeding 80%.
Megakaryocyte deficiency progresses to marrow failure; scoliosis and vertebral abnormalities occur in 30-79%. Nevi alone do not establish skin damage.
Inheritance-based umbrella spanning unrelated organ diseases; no shared organ axis can be assigned from this concept.
Inflammation of the vestibular nerve causes vestibular dysfunction; idiopathic neuritis does not establish infection or autoimmunity.
Placental disease is obstetric and outside the defined organ axes.
Neurodevelopmental disease, mesomelic dysplasia and kidney malformations define KINSSHIP; strabismus occurs in 7/18 (39%). Hypertrichosis does not establish skin damage.
Congenital tibial deficiency and split-hand/foot malformations affect the skeleton; other organ defects are occasional.
RBM20-related isolated dilated cardiomyopathy directly affects myocardium and ventricular function.
The neoplasm occupies the retina, which belongs to the ocular axis.
Deficiency of a coagulation-system protein; associated infections or systemic diseases are causes, not organ involvement of the deficiency.
A primary mixed neuronal-glial tumor arising in the brain.
Primary malignant bone tumor, usually arising in long-bone metaphyses; blood-filled spaces do not make it a blood disease.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability are common; cleft palate and structural pharyngeal abnormalities each occur in 30-79%. Other organ defects are occasional.
Uncharacterized fragile-site/chromosomal entity in the supplied record; no definition or organ phenotype supports a specific axis.
Hereditary neuroendocrine tumors of autonomic paraganglia; hypertension frequency and direct cardiovascular injury are not established.
Chondrodysplasia and polydactyly affect the skeleton; imperforate anus affects the gastrointestinal tract. Situs inversus alone does not establish organ dysfunction.
Skeletal dysplasia; valvular disease, airway obstruction and conductive hearing loss each occur in 30-79%. Skin thickening (30-79%) omitted at the four-axis cap.
Persistent pupillary membrane, megalocornea and developmental cataract are ocular abnormalities.
Anti-HLA alloimmune sensitization is an immune disorder; renal failure and prior transfusions are background conditions, not damage caused by sensitization.
Brain and skin hamartomas define TSC1 disease; renal angiomyolipomas occur in 12/15 (80%). Pulmonary LAM occurs in 20/78 (26%) and is separately diagnosed.
Benign tumor originating in the prostate, a reproductive organ outside the defined axes; urinary tract damage is not established.
